defaults.transcript: (nothing said yet — this is the start of the conversation)
defaults.file_context: (no project files were needed for this request)

orient._comment: List the project every turn because the preceding turn may have changed it. This is evidence for the read-selection pass, not text shown to the user.

ask._comment: No rule lines around the question. A humanDecision prompt is printed by TerminalIO.prompt, not by a renderer, so any banner drawn here survives every display mode and is the one piece of chrome concise mode cannot take back. The question and the caret are the whole prompt.

inspect._comment: A small selection pass copied from coding2's proven read flow. It does not plan or write; it only requests existing files whose current contents are required to answer the current request accurately.

route._comment: Ungated, so it always exists — every other gate in this file reads this one key, and a gate that reads a popped id logs a warning on every turn it is closed. One classifier, one level of gating, no noise.
route.prompt:
The conversation so far:
{transcript}

The person just said:
{user_request}

Would answering this well need looking something up on the web right now?

Answer YES if it turns on something current, local, or specific that a general knowledge of the world would not settle: news, prices, versions and release notes, someone's documentation, a law in a named place, anything that changed recently, or a claim worth checking against a source.

Answer NO if it is settled general knowledge, a matter of reasoning or opinion, a request to write or edit a file, a follow-up about something already in the conversation, or small talk.

When it is genuinely borderline, answer NO. A confident wrong answer is the harm here, and the reply is allowed to say the lookup was not done.

Reply with one word: YES or NO.

lookup.prompt:
The conversation so far:
{transcript}

The person just said:
{user_request}

Write the search query that would find this. Keywords a search engine can use — not a question, not a sentence.

Carry over anything the question depends on that is only in the conversation above: the place, the version, the product, the year. A query missing the one detail that made the question specific finds the wrong thing entirely.

Drop filler: no 'how do I', no 'what is the best', no please. Six words or so.

Reply with the query and nothing else.

lookup._comment: DuckDuckGo, which needs no credentials — clay searches out of the box. This was 'google', and search-keys.json ships blank, so every lookup turn failed the same way: searchWeb refused, web_results came back empty, chosen_urls found nothing to pick and the reply had to admit the lookup did not work. To use Google instead, fill in search-keys.json and change engine to 'google'. apiKey and cx are read only by that engine; they come through {"override": ...} because dispatcher._resolve_action_fields resolves those from raw step_output before the handler runs, and searchWeb does no {placeholder} interpolation on them — an inline template string would arrive at Google literally.

Several URLs, not one. A single pick has no recovery: if that page is a JavaScript shell, paywalled, or moved, the turn has nothing and the reply has to admit the lookup failed. Reading the top few is what a person does — open three tabs — and it costs fetches rather than model calls, because browseWeb reads them all in one action.
lookup.prompt:
The person asked:
{user_request}

Search results:
{web_results}

Pick the results whose pages are most likely to actually answer this — up to three, best first. Reply with one URL per line and nothing else: no numbering, no bullets, no commentary.

Prefer the source over anything written about the source: official documentation, a standards document, the project's own release notes, a government or regulator page, the original announcement. Prefer a page that will contain the specific detail asked for over one that merely covers the topic.

Prefer three different sources over three pages from the same site. The point of reading more than one is that they can disagree, and two pages from one publisher cannot.

Avoid anything that reads as an aggregator, a listicle, a content farm or an advert, however well it matches the words.

One good URL is a fine answer — do not pad to three with pages you do not expect to help.

If the results are empty, or none of them would plausibly answer the question, reply with exactly: NO

lookup._comment: Gated on needs_web rather than on chosen_urls so the gate chain stays one level deep. When chosen_urls came back NO that line is not a URL, browseWeb refuses it on scheme and returns the refusal as the block for it — the reply then sees plainly that a lookup was attempted and found nothing to read, rather than a missing key.

fallback._comment: Runs only on a turn that did not search, and only after the lookup step, so it never overwrites a real result. Skipping the four actions above pops their ids; this puts honest text back under the same names so the answering prompt below never sees an unresolved {placeholder}.

write._comment: Ungated on purpose. A reply with no fences parses to no changes and applyFileWrites returns an empty string without complaint (file_ops.py:856-866), so the ordinary conversational turn costs nothing here and there is no classifier to get wrong.

settle.prompt:
The person said: {user_request}

Should this conversation continue?
Answer NO if they said quit, exit, done, stop, goodbye, bye, or otherwise asked to end it.
Answer YES in every other case.

Reply with one word: YES or NO.
